sentences.text: Long Term Archive is the authoritative repository for Sentinel Vale raw downlink, auxiliary data, processing inputs, generated products, and operational metadata after routine production has completed.
Archive admission begins only after Payload Processing Facility has delivered the product package, associated quality metadata, and checksum evidence required by the configured acceptance rule.
Each accepted object is assigned a persistent identifier that remains stable across media migration, catalogue refresh, and later reprocessing campaigns.
The repository stores object content separately from searchable metadata so that catalogue publication can proceed without exposing internal storage paths.
Catalogue records are published to User Services Portal after Product Quality Service has set the public quality status and the embargo rule has been evaluated.
Products under operational review remain discoverable only to authorized mission staff until the release condition is cleared.
User Services Portal provides search, preview, order, and download functions through a browser interface and documented machine interfaces.
Download services support resumable transfer, integrity verification, and rate controls that protect mission operations from excessive external demand.
Registered users receive authorization scopes based on mission policy, contractual access rights, and applicable data licensing constraints.
Anonymous access is allowed only for product classes that have been approved for open dissemination by mission management.
Long Term Archive retains raw acquisition data for the life of the mission and for the post-mission preservation period defined in the archive policy.
Standard Level 1 and Level 2 products are retained online while demand, contractual latency, or reprocessing dependence justifies low-latency access.
Older product copies may be moved to lower-cost storage when catalogue metadata, checksums, and restore procedures remain available.
Deletion is performed only against superseded temporary products, expired working copies, or objects covered by an approved disposal rule.
Retention exceptions require traceability to the approving authority, the affected product classes, and the expected operational impact.
Reprocessing is triggered when calibration improvements, processor corrections, orbit updates, or quality investigations materially change product fitness for use.
Payload Calibration Team may request a reprocessing campaign when validation evidence shows a systematic radiometric or geometric issue.
Mistral publishes orbit quality state changes to the archive operations queue before catalogue validity flags are updated.
Product Quality Service records the reason for any reprocessing decision so that users can distinguish scientific updates from operational recovery actions.
During reprocessing, Long Term Archive preserves the replaced product version unless the applicable policy allows consolidation after a defined comparison period.
Catalogue records show processing baseline, sensing time, publication time, quality status, and replacement relationships for each released product.
Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Pass Replay Packet to confirm that archived downlink context can support anomaly reconstruction.
External interfaces expose catalogue search, subscription notification, product ordering, and download status using versioned service contracts.
Cybersecurity Desk reviews public interface changes before deployment to confirm authentication, logging, and abuse-control requirements are satisfied.
If Long Term Archive cannot meet a restore or publication commitment, User Services Portal displays a service status message and operations staff open the normal incident process.
